messages.author: bbef7e4b8dc2f6e0
messages.subject: Controlling axes without data loss
parts:
I want a bubble plot of mean length of stay (LOS_mean) by readmission
rate (RR_mean). Each data point is a hospital, and is weighted by the
number of patients seen (RR_N). There are some outliers in the data. A
few hospitals have RR_mean=1 or 0. These hospitals generally have very
few observations (RR_N as small as 1). If I create a subset, with the
restriction RR_N>=100, and plot thusly:

> facility_sub<-subset(facility, RR_N>=100)

> ggplot(facility_sub, aes(LOS_mean, RR_mean, weight=RR_N, size=RR_N)) +
> geom_point() + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=T) +
> opts(legend.position = "none") +
> labs(x="Mean Length of Stay", y="Readmission Rate")

I get (almost; see ** below) the exact plot I would like. However, the
LS fit line and SE are based on the subsetted data. I would like them
to be based on all observations, but to have the window 'zoomed in' on
this portion of the plot. As I undertand it, using the subset (like I
did above) is equivalent to using scale_x/y_continuous() (i.e. throws
out data points that aren't within my limits).


If I plot using the full dataset and utilize coord_cartesian():

> ggplot(facility, aes(LOS_mean, RR_mean, weight=RR_N, size=RR_N)) +
> geom_point() + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=T) +
> opts(legend.position = "none") +
> labs(x="Mean Length of Stay", y="Readmission Rate") +
> coord_cartesian(xlim=c(,10),ylim=c(.03,.19))

I do get a zoomed in view of the data, and the LS fit line and SE are
based on the full data, BUT the y-axis labelling has disappeared and
the backgroud grid squares are now much larger than before. It is
literally like 'looking at the plot under a magnifying glass', to
reference the book. I would like to maintain the look of the first
plot (same axes and axes labels, same grid size in background, etc),
but display the geom_smooth of the full dataset.

Any suggestions? Thanks in advance, Skyler


** I said the first plot gave me *almost* exactly what I wanted
visually. The only complaint was the legend. I decided to just remove
it. The issue I was having is that both the geom_point and geom_smooth
were being forced in the same legend. That is, the legend showed the
weighting used (i.e. a hospital with N observations has a dot 'this
big'), but then on top of the displayed dot, was a big blue line (from
the geom_smooth). I can plot the geom_smooth first, then geom_point,
but this just moves the blue swaths to the background in the legend
(slightly better looking, but still less than ideal), and did the same
in the plot (the line was covered by the data points. I don't want
that to happen). So, essentially, is there a way to have the legend
represent only the geom_point, and NOT the geom_smooth?

It might not be clear from my post:

The majority of the data points in the full dataset are in the range .
04<RR_mean<.18 and 2<LOS_mean<10. The first plot has axes limits that
are almost equivalent to these ranges (i.e. xlim=c(2,10), ylim=c(.
04,.18)) since I am essentially removing all outliers by limiting my
dataset to observations with RR_N>=100. If I were to run the 2nd plot
without the coord_cartesian(), the plot would have axes limits of
xlim=c(0,15), ylim=c(0,1). The majority of the data would be a
cluttered blob in the bottom left portion of the graph.

parts:
Skyjo, 

Really hard to tell without some data to play with, but have you tried giving stat_smooth() your full dataset and geom_point() you subset? 

Something like...

ggplot() +
geom_point(data=facility, aes(LOS_mean, RR_mean, weight=RR_N, size=RR_N)) + geom_smooth(data=facility_sub, aes(LOS_mean, RR_mean), method="lm", se=T) + opts(legend.position = "none") +
labs(x="Mean Length of Stay", y="Readmission Rate")

I can't remember if geom_smooth will cut the range down on it's own or not though. 

brandon

parts: Hi,

On Wed, Oct 27, 2010 at 3:29 PM, skyjo <srjoh...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> Ista Zahn-
>
> 1. You definitey fixed my legend issue. I was unaware of the 'legend='
> argument. This isn't in the book, nor the R help (?geom_smooth), nor
> the online help <http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_smooth.html>. Is there
> another source where I could have found it?
Good question... I picked it up trolling this email list.

>
> 2. I'm 99.9% sure you fixed the axes issue, but just to be explicit:
> Using "scale_x_continuous(limits=)" throws out any data not included
> in the specified limits (I don't want that to happen);

whereas using
> "scale_x_continuous(breaks=)" calculates statistics (i.e. the LS fit
> line and SE) using all the data, but only displays data contained in
> the range of the 'breaks'. True?

Not quite. coord_cartesian(xlim=,ylim=) uses all the data but only
displays data contained in the ranges. scale_x_continuous(breaks=)
and scale_y_continuous(breaks=) tell ggplot where to put the labels on
the x and y axis. Try it and see:

p <- ggplot(data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10), aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point()
p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1,5,10))
p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, 10, by=.5))

Best,
Ista
